actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.

dimensions.assessment: Affects commercial beer brewers who choose to donate spent grain and local agricultural entities receiving the byproduct within a 100-mile radius.
dimensions.evidence: credit against the tax imposed by section 5051 for the calendar year on beer brewed by a brewer

dimensions.assessment: Provides a modest financial incentive ($0.08 per dry weight pound of spent grain) capped at $35,000 per calendar year per brewer.
dimensions.evidence: an amount equal to the product of-- (1) $0.08, multiplied by (2) the number of dry weight pounds of spent grain byproduct

dimensions.assessment: Reduces federal excise tax revenue collected from brewers by an amount up to $35,000 per brewer annually.
dimensions.evidence: for all periods during a calendar year, $35,000.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to establish a new tax credit section and requires recordkeeping and certifications prescribed by the Secretary.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to establish a credit against the excise tax on beer for brewers that donate spent grain

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent ongoing tax credit for beer removed after December 31, 2026.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxes imposed on beer removed after December 31, 2026.

missing_information: Total aggregate macro-level fiscal cost to the federal government.
Number of brewers expected to claim the credit.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates a tax credit against the federal beer excise tax for brewers who donate spent grain for local agricultural use, capped at $35,000 per brewer annually. It affects commercial brewers and local agricultural recipients within a 100-mile radius.

latest_action.text: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
